name: GE (historical Jenbacher gas engine brand, 2003-2018)
description: gas engine / CHP product line (historical ownership) Primary source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenbacher

specifications.metric: GE Energy Jenbacher J920 electrical efficiency (archived GE claim cited by Wikipedia)
specifications.basis: Wikipedia 'Jenbacher' article states 48.7% and cites archived GE Energy pages (gepower.com/prod_serv/products/recip_engines/en/j920.htm archived 2011-01-02; ge-j920gasengine.com archived 2011-03-14). Only the Wikipedia page was read; archived GE pages were not fetched. Page last edited 15 June 2026.
Wikipedia: 'a V20 gas engine delivering up to 9.5 MW (12,915 PS)'. Secondary source; cited to archived GE page.
'When it is put into production it will be Jenbachers most efficient gas engine available with an electrical efficiency of 48.7%'.
'and a combined heat and power (CHP) thermal efficiency of over 90%'.
Wikipedia company history; 'GE (historical Jenbacher gas engine brand, 2003-2018)' corresponds to the GE ownership period.
specifications.value: Founded 1959; acquired by General Electric 2003; became part of INNIO Nov 2018

specifications.basis: Wikipedia 'Company profile and products' and 'Jenbacher J920 FleXtra' sections (some statements carry citation-needed tags).
specifications.value: Otto cycle, industrial spark plugs; smaller models stoichiometric, larger lean-burn with prechamber ignition; Miller cycle and two-stage turbocharging on J920

specifications.basis: Wikipedia: 'Jenbacher engines run on natural gas, landfill gas, sewage gas, biogas, mine gas, coal gas, syngas and hydrogen.'
specifications.value: natural gas, landfill gas, sewage gas, biogas, mine gas, coal gas, syngas and hydrogen
